title: feat: add Scribe realtime transcription
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds paid-only `scribe-realtime` at `/v1/audio/transcriptions/realtime`, routed directly to ElevenLabs `scribe_v2_realtime` with no aliases or fallback.
- Supports the seven confirmed mono PCM/μ-law formats, manual/VAD commits, language controls, partial/final transcripts, timestamps, and background filtering.
- Bills validated decoded audio bytes at ElevenLabs' $0.39/hour rate and settles once on close or error.
- Attaches provider listeners before accepting audio, sanitizes terminal provider errors, rejects malformed query values, and completes close handling safely.
- Keeps premium keyterms/entity detection and media uploads out of scope; live WebSocket chunks do not use `media.pollinations.ai`.

Validation:
- Direct ElevenLabs: every format, manual/VAD, background filtering, and a five-session burst.
- Local Gen E2E: every format, exact transcript/telemetry/ledger billing, malformed input, and clean WebSocket closure. Fresh review-fix probe transcribed 5.247s in 5.738s and billed 0.00056848 Pollen.
- After merging #13320: Gen 50 focused tests and typecheck; Enter 80 pricing/registry tests and typecheck.

Draft for review. The batch-metering prerequisite #13320 is merged and included.

gist.headline: The hive transcribes live
gist.blurb: Scribe Realtime has joined the audio garden. Send it a live audio stream and it returns partial and final transcripts before the sound has properly settled.
gist.summary: Added paid-only `scribe-realtime` WebSocket transcription at `/v1/audio/transcriptions/realtime`, routing directly to ElevenLabs `scribe_v2_realtime` with seven mono PCM/μ-law formats, manual or VAD commits, language controls, timestamps, partial/final transcripts, and background filtering.
gist.impact: Developers can now build live captioning and voice interfaces with streamed transcripts, while validated decoded audio is billed once at ElevenLabs' $0.39/hour rate when the session closes or errors.
gist.visual_concept: Polli is a tiny radio host bee wearing cozy studio headphones, speaking into a retro microphone while glowing sound-wave pixels become neat transcript lines on a CRT terminal. A small Monitor Robot watches partial lines turn into a final checked transcript; potted code-plants and gentle background-filter sparkles make the live audio pipeline feel like a warm little studio.
